title: Verify lore-cli/quest-cli v0.6.0 tag recreation preserves skill content
summary: opum-agent warned: lore-cli and quest-cli are being deleted and recreated tonight (user-authorized, to purge undeletable refs/pull/* refs that served stale CLAUDE.md content). This destroys and recreates the v0.6.0 tag both marketplace.json entries pin, and the recreated tag points at a fresh initial commit (current tree, not the real 0.6.0 release history) -- risking marketplace.json's federated-entry descriptions ('cannot drift from the CLI it describes') becoming quietly false, since check-federated-pins.mjs only checks version match, not content fidelity against a pre-deletion baseline.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Before either deletion: capture a verifiable baseline for both repos' v0.6.0 -- full ref chain (tag object -> commit -> tree -> named subtrees for .claude-plugin/ and skills/), plus the actual tarball bytes, since a hash alone can't be resolved back into content once the source is deleted. Done: baseline-lore-v0.6.0.tar.gz (3.07MB), baseline-quest-v0.6.0.tar.gz (199.9MB), full chain recorded.

quest-cli's recreated v0.6.0 verified directly against the live repo (not taken from any relay, including a well-evidenced one) -- full ref chain re-resolved myself: tag object f1a75ab4 -> commit a9fbc78a -> skills subtree 633c776b (EXACT match to baseline, byte-identical) -> .claude-plugin subtree 22885902 (differs from baseline 393318c5). plugin.json content pulled directly: only author.name changed, 'Opum' -> 'Opum AI' -- the OPAG-70 branding pass, landed correctly per the fleet's own naming taxonomy (Opum AI = company). Nothing else in plugin.json changed; version still 0.6.0, matching its own tag name.

Decide whether marketplace.json needs an edit for quest-cli's entry, given the finding. It does not: this repo's opum-quest entry already reads author.name 'Opum AI' (OMARK-37) -- manifest and plugin now agree, where they briefly would not have. Source pins by tag NAME ('ref': 'v0.6.0'), not a SHA, so tag recreation under the same name needed no marketplace-side change for federation to keep resolving. The description's 'cannot drift' claim survives in substance: the skill content itself (skills/) is unchanged.

lore-cli's side: same live verification, once its own deletion/recreation actually happens -- not assumed to match quest-cli's outcome just because the pattern held once. lore-cli's v0.6.0 is still untouched as of this check (tag object 5162575, unchanged), held at its user's own prompt on an unrelated npm publishing question. This criterion stays open until that happens.
